description.narrative: Stöd till entreprenörer i postkonflikt länder genom Africa Enterprise Challenge Fund. Länder som tillhör målgruppen är Liberia, Somalia, DRC, Sierra Leone och Zimbabwe genom ett seperat fönster.
Support to a conflict window of the African Agribusiness Enterprise Challenge Fund. Countries targeted are Liberia, Somalia, DRC, Sierra Leone and Zimbabwe which is handled through a spereate window.

The Post Conflict Window (PCW) is a special funding window for inclusive business in agribusiness, agribusiness value chains, and rural financial services in conflict-affected countries. The objective of the intervention is to develop agribusiness and rural finance market systems to benefit the lives of poor rural households across Africa. PCW provides investment support to companies in order to enable them to carry out new and innovative initiatives within the fields of agriculture, rural financing, renewable energy and adaptation to climate change for smallholders in rural Africa. This contribution, the PCW, was designed to provide a positive contribution to pro-poor growth in Sub-Saharan Africa by encouraging private sector investments specifically in the agriculture sectors of African countries emerging from conflict, such as Somalia, Democratic Republic of Congo, Liberia and Sierra Leone.

Out of the 187 applications to AECF post-conflict window, nineteen investees were supported throughout this program. As a result, AECF assesses that some 72 286 households have been impacted by the programme, out of which 76% live in rural areas, whereas the initial target was 100 000 households. This amounts to 361 430 individuals, whereas the original target was 500 000. However, 5896 jobs have been created, whereas the target was 3100. Another indicator that was widely surpassed is the development rate of return, which is assessed to be 10.2 (as opposed to the planned 1.0). It is assessed that a cumulative USD 115 795 404 has been generated throughout the project implementation. The AECF portfolio under this window, managed to attract matching funds from third parties, leveraging a cumulative USD 24 million at the end of the program. Results show that agro-processors that set up processing plants and developed linkages with outgrowers were successful in substituting imported products in their respective markets, contributing to private sector development in post-conflict countries. Another clear result was that the micro-finance institutions supported in Somaliland were shown to be additional and effective despite the perceived high risk profile. One learning is that by designing faith-sensitive loan products that were Sharia compliant, acceptability rates and uptake was increased.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
